rows.name: Air
rows.blurb: Invisible, but made of atoms and molecules.

composition.note: by far the most common gas

rows.fun_fact: Most of the air is nitrogen, not oxygen. Nitrogen also dilutes oxygen, which slows burning.

rows.name: A banana
rows.blurb: Sweet, soft and a good source of potassium.

composition.note: a mineral found in many foods

rows.fun_fact: A tiny part of all natural potassium is radioactive potassium-40, so food with potassium holds a trace of it. So does your own body.

rows.name: A diamond
rows.blurb: A crystal made of carbon atoms.

composition.note: the only element in a diamond

rows.fun_fact: In a diamond, every carbon atom is bonded to its neighbours in one giant network. Chemists call that a covalent network solid.

rows.name: A gold bar
rows.blurb: Pure gold is just one kind of atom.

composition.note: the only element in pure gold

rows.fun_fact: Gold is an element, so it cannot be broken down into anything simpler. A bar of pure gold holds nothing but gold atoms.

rows.name: A blade of grass
rows.blurb: Grass makes its own food from sunlight, air and water.

composition.note: from carbon dioxide in the air

rows.fun_fact: A plant builds sugar out of carbon dioxide and water. Much of the carbon in a blade of grass was once part of the air.

rows.name: A strand of hair
rows.blurb: Hair is a filament of keratin, a protein.
rows.fun_fact: Every protein contains nitrogen, and many contain sulfur, together with carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Keratin is a protein.

rows.name: Your hand
rows.blurb: Your body is made of the same elements as everything else.
rows.fun_fact: Oxygen, carbon, hydrogen and nitrogen are the four most abundant elements in the human body.

rows.name: A red blood cell
rows.blurb: A cell that carries oxygen around your body.
rows.fun_fact: Hemoglobin, the molecule that carries oxygen in your blood, is made of proteins and iron.

rows.name: A grain of rice
rows.blurb: Mostly starch, a long chain of sugar molecules.

composition.note: in the sugar chains of starch

rows.fun_fact: Glucose, a sugar your body uses for fuel, is made of just carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Starch is glucose joined in long chains.

rows.name: Table salt
rows.blurb: A shake of salt from the kitchen.
rows.fun_fact: Sodium and chlorine can react to form table salt. Joined together they are nothing like what they were on their own.

rows.name: The Sun
rows.blurb: A hot, glowing ball of gas: our nearest star.

composition.note: fused into helium in the core
made from hydrogen in the core

rows.fun_fact: In the Sun's core, hydrogen is fused into helium. Those nuclear reactions power its heat and light.

rows.name: A glass of water
rows.blurb: Every drop is made of the same tiny molecules.
rows.fun_fact: Water is always two hydrogen atoms for every oxygen atom, in a glass, a lake or a cloud.
